provider:claude.title: Claude
provider:claude.text: Uses a Claude plan, signed in through Claude's own app on the computer that does the work. The Anthropic API is a separate, pay-as-you-go choice.
provider:claude.expert: Claude Code CLI with its own browser sign-in (Claude plan, Console or company SSO); the CLI keeps its sign-in on the execution host. The Anthropic API is a separate provider billed per token.

provider:codex.title: ChatGPT / Codex
provider:codex.text: Two ways in: sign in with ChatGPT to use your plan's limits, or use an OpenAI API key, billed separately by use. Each one is its own account here.
provider:codex.expert: Direct provider with two auth families: ChatGPT OAuth (plan-backed usage) or an OpenAI API key (API billing). Separate account rows; their usage and cooldowns never merge.

provider:antigravity.title: Google Antigravity
provider:antigravity.text: Uses your Google Antigravity account, through Google's own app on the computer that does the work. The Gemini API is a separate choice.
provider:antigravity.expert: Antigravity CLI (agy) with Google sign-in; the CLI keeps its sign-in on the execution host, and on a remote host uses its sign-in link and returned code. Gemini API is a separate provider.

provider:cursor.title: Cursor
provider:cursor.text: Paste an API key from your Cursor dashboard. It uses your Cursor plan.
provider:cursor.expert: Cursor SDK route with a user or service-account API key from the Cursor dashboard; Team Admin keys aren't accepted. Browser sign-in through cursor-agent is the other way in.

provider:grok.title: Grok Build
provider:grok.text: Uses Grok Build, signed in through xAI's own app on the computer that does the work. The xAI API is a separate, pay-as-you-go choice.
provider:grok.expert: Grok Build CLI (grok) with xAI browser sign-in, or a device code when the browser is on another device; the CLI keeps its sign-in. The xAI API is a separate provider.

provider:muse.title: Muse Code
provider:muse.text: Uses Muse Code, signed in through Meta's own app. That sign-in works only in Muse Code; other Meta keys are billed separately.
provider:muse.expert: Muse Code CLI (muse) with its own sign-in; the subscription credential is limited to Muse Code, and an API key set in Muse takes precedence over it. The Meta Model API is separate.

provider:copilot.title: GitHub Copilot
provider:copilot.text: Signs in with your GitHub account, then asks whose Copilot plan to use: yours or an organization's. It doesn't change where your code is kept.
provider:copilot.expert: GitHub Copilot direct hosted API: GitHub OAuth, then entitlement and billing-entity selection before Ready. Separate from the GitHub account used for repositories.

provider:qwen-coding.title: Alibaba Coding Plan
provider:qwen-coding.text: Alibaba Cloud's Coding Plan, with Qwen and other models. It needs the plan's own key, not an ordinary Alibaba Cloud key. A plan bought for China is set up in Settings.
provider:qwen-coding.expert: Alibaba Coding Plan: dedicated plan key (sk-sp-…) on the global endpoint; not interchangeable with DashScope pay-as-you-go keys. The China route is in Settings.

provider:qwen-token.title: Alibaba Token Plan
provider:qwen-token.text: Alibaba Cloud's Token Plan, a monthly plan. It has its own key, separate from the Coding Plan.
provider:qwen-token.expert: Alibaba Model Studio Token Plan: a subscription (Personal or Team edition) with its own key; separate from Coding Plan and from pay-as-you-go.

provider:zai.title: Z.AI Coding Plan
provider:zai.text: Z.AI's monthly plan for coding, with GLM models. It connects with a key from your Z.AI account. A plan bought for China (Zhipu) is set up in Settings.
provider:zai.expert: Z.AI GLM Coding Plan with an API key on the coding endpoint. Zhipu's China plan is a separate route, in Settings.

provider:kimi.title: Kimi Code
provider:kimi.text: Kimi Code's monthly plan. Get the key from the Kimi Code console; a Kimi Open Platform key is a different, pay-as-you-go account.
provider:kimi.expert: Kimi For Coding direct route with a Kimi Code console key, separate from Moonshot Open Platform keys; Puppet Master sends its own client identity.

provider:minimax.title: MiniMax M Plan
provider:minimax.text: MiniMax's monthly plan, now called M Plan (it was the Coding Plan). It needs the plan's own key. A plan bought for China is set up in Settings.
provider:minimax.expert: MiniMax M Plan (formerly Coding Plan): plan key on the global (minimax.io) endpoint; a pay-as-you-go MiniMax key isn't plan access. The China route is in Settings.

provider:opencode-go.title: OpenCode Go
provider:opencode-go.text: OpenCode's monthly plan, used with a key from the OpenCode Console.
provider:opencode-go.expert: OpenCode Go subscription key from the OpenCode Console. Not the OpenCode server.

provider:opencode-zen.title: OpenCode Console
provider:opencode-zen.text: OpenCode's pay-as-you-go service, which used to be called Zen. You buy credit in the OpenCode Console, then use its key.
provider:opencode-zen.expert: OpenCode Console (formerly Zen): a pay-as-you-go gateway funded by Console credit, with an API key; not the OpenCode server connection.

provider:opencode-runtime.title: OpenCode server
provider:opencode-runtime.text: Uses OpenCode itself as a server. Puppet Master can run it for you, or connect to one you already run. Its own model accounts stay in OpenCode.
provider:opencode-runtime.expert: OpenCode server profile: Managed Server (launched on the execution host) or Attach to Existing Server (endpoint plus optional HTTP Basic auth). Upstream auth stays in OpenCode.

provider:anthropic-api.title: Anthropic API
provider:anthropic-api.text: Pay as you go with Anthropic, using a key from the Claude Console. Separate from a Claude plan.
provider:anthropic-api.expert: Anthropic API key (sk-ant-…) from the Claude Console, billed per token. A key that isn't tied to one workspace asks which workspace to use.

provider:gemini-api.title: Gemini API
provider:gemini-api.text: Google's Gemini through a key from Google AI Studio. Separate from Antigravity.
provider:gemini-api.expert: Gemini Direct (API key only) from AI Studio; the key's Cloud project decides its free or paid tier and quota. Separate from Antigravity.

provider:vertex.title: Vertex AI
provider:vertex.text: Google's AI through your Google Cloud account, billed by Google Cloud. Pick it if your work already uses Google Cloud.
provider:vertex.expert: Vertex AI with a Google Cloud API key, in express mode or tied to a project; billing and quota follow that project.

provider:xai-api.title: xAI API
provider:xai-api.text: Pay as you go with xAI, using a key from the xAI Console. Separate from a Grok Build plan.
provider:xai-api.expert: xAI API key from the xAI Console, billed per request. Separate from Grok Build.

provider:meta-api.title: Meta Model API
provider:meta-api.text: Pay as you go with Meta's models, using a key from Meta's developer site. A Muse Code plan's sign-in is different.
provider:meta-api.expert: Meta Model API key from dev.meta.ai, billed by use. The Muse Code subscription credential works only in Muse Code.

pairing:approval.title: Approve from another device
pairing:approval.text: A device you already use with it shows a request, and you approve it there. The quickest way when that device is with you.
pairing:approval.expert: Pairing by approval: an already trusted device receives the request and approves it; this device is then trusted by the Server.

pairing:code.title: Enter the code it shows
pairing:code.text: Open your Puppet Master's page on the other computer, read the code it shows and type it here. Good when no other device is at hand.
pairing:code.expert: Pairing by code: the Server's page shows a short one-time code; entering it here proves this device is with you before it is trusted.

pairing:qr.title: Scan its QR code
pairing:qr.text: Point this device's camera at the square code on the other screen. Handy on a phone or tablet.
pairing:qr.expert: Pairing by QR code: the camera reads the one-time pairing code from the other screen.

field:headscale.title: Headscale address
field:headscale.text: The web address of your own Headscale server, starting with https://. Only for people who run Headscale instead of using a Tailscale account.
field:headscale.expert: The https URL of your Headscale control server (a self-hosted Tailscale control plane). Leave it to Tailscale accounts unless you run Headscale.

field:acc-bucket.title: Bucket
field:acc-bucket.text: The bucket's name, and a folder in it if you like, such as my-backups/puppet-master. A bucket is storage space you rent from a cloud company.
field:acc-bucket.expert: The bucket, optionally /prefix, checked with the chosen service's bucket-name rule (Amazon and Backblaze differ).

field:acc-keyId.title: Access key ID
field:acc-keyId.text: The ID half of the key made for the bucket. Copy it from your storage account; the secret below is its password.
field:acc-keyId.expert: The access key ID (Backblaze: application key ID) of a key scoped to that bucket.

field:acc-secret.title: Secret
field:acc-secret.text: The private half of that key. Kept in your computer's password store, never in Puppet Master's files.
field:acc-secret.expert: The secret access key (Backblaze: application key). Stored in the OS keychain, never in Puppet Master's files or logs.

field:acc-address.title: Server address
field:acc-address.text: Where the backup goes on that server: start it with sftp:// for SFTP, or https:// for WebDAV, then the folder.
field:acc-address.expert: The server's URL with the backup path: sftp:// for SFTP, https:// for WebDAV, matching the protocol chosen above.

field:acc-user.title: Username
field:acc-user.text: The name you sign in with on that backup server.
field:acc-user.expert: The account name on the SFTP or WebDAV server.

field:acc-password.title: Password
field:acc-password.text: The password for that backup server. Kept in your computer's password store, never in Puppet Master's files.
field:acc-password.expert: The account's password on that server. Stored in the OS keychain, never in Puppet Master's files.

field:key.title: API key
field:key.text: A long secret code from the AI company, not your password. Paste it, then choose Check key. It's kept in the keychain on the computer that does the work.
field:key.expert: The route's own API key, checked against the provider before it is saved; stored in the OS keychain on the execution host, never in Puppet Master's files.

tour.title: Take the Guided Tour
tour.text: A few minutes, with a practice example, so nothing real changes. Pick it if Puppet Master is new to you.

enter.title: Enter Puppet Master
enter.text: Closes setup and opens Puppet Master now. You can start the Guided Tour any time from Settings.

startOver.title: Start over
startOver.text: Clears the choices from last time and begins setup again from the first page.

way:codex|main.title: Sign in with ChatGPT
way:codex|main.text: Uses your ChatGPT plan. Codex use counts against that plan's limits.
way:codex|main.expert: ChatGPT OAuth account row; plan-backed usage bucket.

way:codex|alt.title: Use an OpenAI API key
way:codex|alt.text: A key from the OpenAI API dashboard. Billed by use, separately from any ChatGPT plan.
way:codex|alt.expert: API-key account row at standard API pricing, separate from ChatGPT plan usage.

way:cursor|main.title: Use a Cursor API key
way:cursor|main.text: Make a key in your Cursor dashboard under API Keys, then paste it here.
way:cursor|main.expert: Cursor SDK with a user or service-account API key; no CLI needed.

way:cursor|alt.title: Sign in in the browser instead
way:cursor|alt.text: Installs Cursor's command-line tool on the computer that does the work, then you sign in to Cursor in your browser.
way:cursor|alt.expert: cursor-agent login in a Puppet Master profile root on the execution host; needs the CLI installed.

field:paste.title: Code from the page
field:paste.text: After you sign in on the company's page, it shows a code. Paste it here so the sign-in reaches the computer that does the work.
field:paste.expert: One-use return code for the sign-in on the execution host; read once, never saved.

field:project.title: Google Cloud project ID
field:project.text: The project your key belongs to, if it belongs to one. It decides which Google Cloud bill pays.
field:project.expert: Optional project ID for billing and quota; leave empty for an express-mode key.

field:ocAddr.title: Server address
field:ocAddr.text: The web address your OpenCode server answers on. On the same computer it's often http://127.0.0.1:4096.
field:ocAddr.expert: Base URL of the running opencode serve (default 127.0.0.1:4096).

field:ocUser.title: Username
field:ocUser.text: Only if your OpenCode server asks for one. It's usually opencode.

field:ocPass.title: Password
field:ocPass.text: Only if your OpenCode server has a password. It's the server's own password, not a key from an AI company.
field:ocPass.expert: HTTP Basic password (OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD); kept in the OS keychain, separate from model-provider keys.

group:entity.title: Whose Copilot plan
group:entity.text: Copilot can come with your own GitHub plan or an organization's. Pick the one that should pay.
group:entity.expert: Copilot billing entity; entitlement and premium-request limits follow it.

group:workspace.title: Workspace
group:workspace.text: Anthropic bills each workspace separately. Pick the one this key's use should go to.
group:workspace.expert: Workspace context for a key that isn't scoped to one workspace.

ocMode:managed.title: Let Puppet Master run it
ocMode:managed.text: Puppet Master installs OpenCode if needed, starts it and keeps it running on the computer that does the work.
ocMode:managed.expert: Managed Server profile: Puppet Master owns launch, config root, reconnect and shutdown.

ocMode:attached.title: Use a server I already run
ocMode:attached.text: For an OpenCode server you started yourself. Puppet Master connects to it and leaves its settings to you.
ocMode:attached.expert: Attach to Existing Server: Puppet Master owns the endpoint, its auth and health checks only; the server's own settings stay External / Not Managed.

field:acc-session.title: Session token
field:acc-session.text: Only for temporary keys: the third part they come with. Kept in your computer's password store.
field:acc-session.expert: The STS session token that temporary AWS credentials require. Stored with the secret, never in files or logs.

field:acc-b2host.title: S3 address
field:acc-b2host.text: The bucket's S3 address, shown on its page in Backblaze, like s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com.
field:acc-b2host.expert: Backblaze B2's regional S3 address, s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com.

field:acc-server.title: Service address
field:acc-server.text: The S3 address your storage service gives you, starting with https://.

field:acc-region.title: Region
field:acc-region.text: Only if your storage service asks for one. Leave it empty otherwise.
field:acc-region.expert: The signing region, for services that require one; empty uses the service's default.

lookMenu.title: Change the look
lookMenu.text: Opens the looks right here, without leaving setup. Your choices so far are kept.

sound.title: Sound
sound.text: Turns setup's sounds and Pip's voice on or off. Nothing plays until you click or press a key.

close.title: Close
close.text: Your choices are saved. Finish setting up brings you back to where you left off.

resume.title: Finish setting up
resume.text: Opens setup again where you left off. Every choice you made is still there.

lookFamily:basic.title: Basic
lookFamily:basic.text: A clean diagram: plain shapes, calm and precise movement, quiet sounds. The calmest look.

lookFamily:friendly.title: Friendly
lookFamily:friendly.text: Warm colours, rounded shapes and playful movement, like a little paper theatre. The cosiest look.

lookFamily:glass.title: Glass
lookFamily:glass.text: Frosted glass over soft, moving light. Settings choose how see-through the panels are; text always stays readable.

lookFamily:retro.title: Retro
lookFamily:retro.text: Pixel-sharp, like an old computer. Dark is a glowing green screen; Light looks printed on paper.

lookFamily:nier.title: NieR
lookFamily:nier.text: Ink and parchment inspired by NieR: Automata, with square lines, its own sounds and a scene behind the app. Adjust NieR chooses which of its pieces you want.

lookMode:light.title: Light or dark
lookMode:light.text: Every look has a light and a dark version. First-time setup starts in Basic Dark; choose whichever is easier for you to read.

lookMode:dark.title: Light or dark
lookMode:dark.text: Every look has a light and a dark version. First-time setup starts in Basic Dark; choose whichever is easier for you to read.

lookNier:nier.title: NieR
lookNier:nier.text: An ink-and-parchment look inspired by NieR: Automata, in light and dark like every look. Adjust NieR chooses its pieces.

lookNierAdjust:nier-adjust.title: Adjust NieR
lookNierAdjust:nier-adjust.text: Choose which pieces of NieR you want, like its menu sounds, its motion and the picture behind it.

skipAll.title: Skip
skipAll.text: Closes setup and opens Puppet Master as it is. Run Onboarding Again in Settings brings setup back any time.

pickFamily:basic.title: Basic
pickFamily:basic.text: A clean diagram: plain shapes, calm and precise movement, quiet sounds. The calmest look.

pickFamily:friendly.title: Friendly
pickFamily:friendly.text: Warm colours, rounded shapes and playful movement, like a little paper theatre. The cosiest look.

pickFamily:glass.title: Glass
pickFamily:glass.text: Frosted glass over soft, moving light. Settings choose how see-through the panels are; text always stays readable.

pickFamily:retro.title: Retro
pickFamily:retro.text: Pixel-sharp, like an old computer. Dark is a glowing green screen; Light looks printed on paper.

pickFamily:nier.title: NieR
pickFamily:nier.text: Ink and parchment inspired by NieR: Automata, with square lines, its own sounds and a scene behind the app. Adjust NieR chooses which of its pieces you want.

group:pickMode.title: Light or dark
group:pickMode.text: Every look has a light and a dark version. First-time setup starts in Basic Dark; choose whichever is easier for you to read.

pickNier.title: NieR
pickNier.text: An ink-and-parchment look inspired by NieR: Automata, in light and dark like every look. Adjust NieR chooses its pieces.

adjustNier.title: Adjust NieR
adjustNier.text: Choose which pieces of NieR you want, like its menu sounds, its motion and the picture behind it.

pick:this.title: This computer
pick:this.text: Puppet Master does the work on this computer. The AI, an online copy and a backup are separate choices, made next.
pick:this.expert: Puppet Master runs on this computer: Projects, local history and agent runs are here. AI providers, online copies and backups are the services you choose.

pick:connect.title: Connect this device
pick:connect.text: Already use Puppet Master on another computer? This device joins it and uses its Projects and AI. You confirm it is really you, once.
pick:connect.expert: This device becomes a client of an existing Puppet Master Server: it uses that Server's Projects, runs and AI accounts after a one-time pairing.

pick:server.title: Server
pick:server.text: A Server is a separate computer that stays switched on and does the work, like a NAS or a rented cloud computer. Your laptop and other devices connect to it, and it can keep working while they sleep.
pick:server.expert: A Server is a separate, always-on machine (a NAS, a rented cloud machine or a spare computer) that runs Puppet Master and its agent runs; this computer and your other devices pair with it as clients.

restoreAll.title: Restore everything
restoreAll.text: For moving from an old computer: brings back your Projects, settings and look from a backup. Nothing here is replaced without asking.
restoreAll.expert: Restores a full backup (Projects, settings, look) from a Recovery Kit or a backup destination onto this computer, with a preview before anything changes.

group:pickServer.title: Found on your network
group:pickServer.text: Puppet Masters already running on your network. Pick the one this device should use. You'll see its Projects once this device is paired with it.
group:pickServer.expert: Puppet Master Servers found by discovery on your local network, and on a VPN you're connected to. Discovery shows only a name, an address and an ID; Project details come after pairing.

field:addr.title: Its address
field:addr.text: The name or number other devices use to reach it, like home-nas.local or 192.168.1.20. Use it when yours is not in the list.
field:addr.expert: The Server's hostname or IP address on your network, like home-nas.local or 192.168.1.20.

manualOn.title: Enter an address instead
manualOn.text: Type the address yourself when your Puppet Master does not show up on its own.
manualOn.expert: Enter the Server's hostname or IP address yourself when discovery doesn't find it.

route:local_or_vpn.title: On this network
route:local_or_vpn.text: Finds it on the network you are on now. You can connect through a VPN too: Puppet Masters there show up as well.
route:local_or_vpn.expert: Local network or an already connected VPN: discovery on the LAN, and on the VPN's networks.

route:tailscale.title: Tailscale
route:tailscale.text: Reach it from anywhere with Tailscale, a private network for your own devices. It's built into Puppet Master: sign in once.
route:tailscale.expert: Tailscale is built into Puppet Master's apps: sign in once with your Tailscale account. A plain browser tab reaches it with a Remote Link, or with the device's own Tailscale.

route:reverse_proxy.title: My own web address
route:reverse_proxy.text: For a Server its owner already put on a web address, like pm.example.com. Pick it only if you were given one.
route:reverse_proxy.expert: The Server behind a reverse proxy on an https domain its owner set up (DNS and a TLS certificate). The certificate protects the connection; it doesn't vouch for who runs the address.

route:remote_link.title: Puppet Master Remote Link
route:remote_link.text: A private link your Server can make for you. Paste the link it gave you; nothing else to set up.
route:remote_link.expert: A Puppet Master Remote Link the Server issues for reaching it from outside your network; paste it here. Nothing to set up on your side: no DNS, ports or certificates.

tsControl:hosted.title: Tailscale account
tsControl:hosted.text: Sign in with an ordinary Tailscale account. Right for nearly everyone.
tsControl:hosted.expert: Tailscale's hosted coordination server with an ordinary Tailscale account.

tsControl:headscale.title: My own Headscale server
tsControl:headscale.text: Headscale is a version of Tailscale you run yourself. Pick it only if you already have one.
tsControl:headscale.expert: A self-hosted Headscale control server instead of Tailscale's; you'll give its https URL.

field:proxy.title: Web address
field:proxy.text: The https:// address the Server owner set up, like https://pm.example.com.
field:proxy.expert: The reverse proxy's https URL for the Server, like https://pm.example.com.

field:link.title: Remote Link or its code
field:link.text: The link your Server made, or the short code it shows. Your Server shows them in Settings › Server & Project Location › Away From Home.
field:link.expert: The Server-issued Remote Link (or its short code) from Settings › Server & Project Location › Away From Home; pairing still follows.

field:code.title: Code from your Puppet Master
field:code.text: The 8 letters and numbers its page shows, like A7K9-M2Q4. It proves this device is with you.
field:code.expert: The one-time pairing code the Server's page shows (8 characters, like A7K9-M2Q4).

resend.title: Send a new one
resend.text: Ends the request that went missing and sends a fresh one. Only the new one can be approved.
resend.expert: Cancels the current pairing request and starts a new one; an answer to the old request is ignored.

createNew.title: Create a new Project
createNew.text: Starts a new Project on your Puppet Master, so it lives next to the work.
createNew.expert: Starts a new Project draft on the connected Server; its files and runs live on the Server.

group:pickProject.title: Projects on your Puppet Master
group:pickProject.text: Projects it already has. Pick one to open first; every one of them is there for you later too.
group:pickProject.expert: The Server's existing Projects; the one you pick opens first.

kind:nas.title: A NAS or home server
kind:nas.text: A storage box or home server that stays on, like Synology, TrueNAS, Unraid or QNAP. A good home for a Server.
kind:nas.expert: A NAS or home server (Synology, TrueNAS, Unraid, QNAP) running Puppet Master's Server; always on, on your LAN.

kind:cloud.title: A cloud computer
kind:cloud.text: A computer you rent online. It is always on and costs a monthly fee. You make it yours with a one-time code from your cloud provider's console, so nothing is set up over the open internet.
kind:cloud.expert: A rented cloud VM running the Server, claimed with the one-time setup code from the provider console; no public setup endpoint. Public access is a separate, later choice.

kind:pc.title: Another computer
kind:pc.text: A Windows, Mac or Linux computer you leave switched on. Fine if it does not sleep.
kind:pc.expert: A Windows, macOS or Linux machine running the Server; it must stay on and not sleep.

group:platform.title: Install Puppet Master on it
group:platform.text: Pick what that computer runs, and follow its steps there. It shows up here by itself once it is running.
group:platform.expert: Install the Server package for that machine's platform; it shows up here by itself once it is running.

copy:install.title: Copy the install line
copy:install.text: Copies the line to paste into a terminal on that computer. A terminal is the window where you type commands.
copy:install.expert: Copies the install command for that machine's terminal (shell).

group:guide.title: Open the install guide
group:guide.text: Opens the step-by-step guide for that system in your browser.
group:guide.expert: Opens the official install guide for that platform.

group:pick.title: Waiting to be set up
group:pick.text: A computer on your network running Puppet Master that is not set up yet. Choose it to make it your Server.
group:pick.expert: An unclaimed Puppet Master Server found on your network; choosing it starts the claim.

field:addr.title: Its address
field:addr.text: Where to reach it, if it doesn't show up by itself. A cloud computer needs no address: you use the setup code from your provider's console.
field:addr.expert: The Server's hostname or IP on your network. A cloud VM is claimed with the one-time code its provider console shows, not by address.

manualOn.title: Enter its address instead
manualOn.text: Type its address yourself if it does not appear on its own.
manualOn.expert: Enter the Server's hostname or IP address yourself.

field:name.title: Name
field:name.text: What you'll call this Server everywhere in Puppet Master, like Home NAS. Pick a name you'll recognise.
field:name.expert: The Server's display name across your devices.

group:suggest.title: Suggested names
group:suggest.text: A few names that fit this kind of computer. Pick one, or type your own.
group:suggest.expert: Suggested display names for this kind of machine; pick one or type your own.

field:code.title: Setup code
field:code.text: The one-time number shown on the Server's own setup page, or for a cloud computer in your provider's console, like 482 913. It proves the computer is yours.
field:code.expert: The one-time setup code from the Server's setup page (a cloud VM: the provider console); it proves physical or console access before the claim.

selfMatch.title: The words match
selfMatch.text: Tick this only when the words here are the same as on this device. Nothing is paired until you approve.
selfMatch.expert: Confirms the identity words shown here match this device's, so the pairing goes to the right device.

newCode.title: New code
newCode.text: Makes a fresh code for adding a device. Devices already paired stay paired.
newCode.expert: Rotates the device invite code; already paired devices keep their trust.

copy:pairlink.title: Copy the link
copy:pairlink.text: Copies the link to this Server at the address it was found at, for another device on the same network to open and ask to join.
copy:pairlink.expert: Copies the pairing URL at the Server's reached address; the joining device still needs your approval.

group:approve.title: Approve
group:approve.text: Lets that device use your Server. Approve only once its words match what the device shows.
group:approve.expert: Approves the device's pairing request after its identity words match: it becomes a trusted client.

group:deny.title: Deny
group:deny.text: Turns the request down. Nothing is shared with that device.
group:deny.expert: Rejects the pairing request; no trust or data is shared.

group:match.title: The words match
group:match.text: Compare the words with what the other device shows, then tick this. It unlocks Approve.
group:match.expert: Confirms the device's identity words match; required before Approve.

restore.title: Bring back old data
restore.text: Replacing an old Server? Brings its Projects back from a Recovery Kit or an old backup.
restore.expert: Restores Projects onto this new Server from a Recovery Kit or a backup destination.

source:kit.title: A Recovery Kit file
source:kit.text: The file you saved when you set up backups. It is not a place: it says where your backup is kept and holds the key that unlocks it, so there is no phrase to type. It never holds a NAS or cloud sign-in. The best place to start.
source:kit.expert: The Recovery Kit file from your backup setup: the destination hints and the Backup Recovery Key for its backup repository. Opening it points to the backup and unlocks it; it holds no NAS, cloud or other service credential.

group:kit.title: Which Recovery Kit
group:kit.text: Recovery Kit files found on this computer. Pick the one for the backup you want back.
group:kit.expert: Recovery Kit files found in the usual places on this computer (Downloads, Documents, the Desktop).

group:bfolder.title: Which folder
group:bfolder.text: Folders on this computer or a plugged-in drive that hold a Puppet Master backup.
group:bfolder.expert: Folders on this computer or a mounted drive that contain a Puppet Master backup repository.

field:bpath.title: Where the backup folder is
field:bpath.text: The folder's full location, as your file browser shows it.
field:bpath.expert: The backup repository's folder path, as your file manager shows it.

source:folder.title: A folder on this computer
source:folder.text: A backup kept on this computer, or on a drive you plugged in. You point to the folder next; the recovery phrase from your Recovery Kit unlocks it.
source:folder.expert: A backup repository in a local folder or on a mounted drive. You point to the folder next; the Backup Recovery Key from your Recovery Kit unlocks it.

source:nas.title: A NAS or another computer
source:nas.text: A backup kept on a NAS or another computer. Puppet Master reaches it over a secure connection (SSH).
source:nas.expert: A backup repository on a NAS or another computer, reached over SSH (host identity check, then a key).

source:cloud.title: A cloud account
source:cloud.text: A backup kept in Google Drive, OneDrive or a storage bucket. Only backups kept there are shown next.
source:cloud.expert: Google Drive, OneDrive or an S3-family bucket; the snapshot list is scoped to the exact service, account and bucket reached.

group:device.title: Which device
group:device.text: Devices on your network that can be reached securely. Pick the one that keeps the backup.
group:device.expert: Devices on your network with SSH enabled. Pick the one holding the backup repository.

cloud:gdrive.title: Google Drive
cloud:gdrive.text: You sign in to Google on its own page next. Puppet Master only reads the backup.
cloud:gdrive.expert: Google Drive through Google's own sign-in (OAuth), read-only for the restore.

cloud:onedrive.title: OneDrive
cloud:onedrive.text: You sign in to Microsoft on its own page next. Puppet Master only reads the backup.
cloud:onedrive.expert: OneDrive through Microsoft's own sign-in (OAuth), read-only for the restore.

cloud:s3.title: A storage bucket
cloud:s3.text: A bucket on Amazon S3, Backblaze B2 or another S3-compatible service. Pick which, then fill in its access details below.
cloud:s3.expert: An S3-family bucket (aws_s3, backblaze_b2 or s3_compatible) reached with its own access details; only backups in that exact bucket are listed next.

rsub:aws_s3.title: Amazon S3
rsub:aws_s3.text: Amazon's storage. You need the bucket's name and an access key made for it.
rsub:aws_s3.expert: AWS S3: bucket name (3-63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes), region discovered from the bucket; access key ID and secret, plus a session token for temporary credentials.

rsub:backblaze_b2.title: Backblaze B2
rsub:backblaze_b2.text: Backblaze's storage. You need the bucket's S3 address, shown on its page, and an application key made for that bucket.
rsub:backblaze_b2.expert: Backblaze B2 through its S3-compatible API: s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com, an application key ID and key (the master application key is refused there); bucket names 6-63 characters.

rsub:s3_compatible.title: S3-compatible storage
rsub:s3_compatible.text: Any other storage that works like Amazon's, such as Wasabi or MinIO. You need its address, the bucket and a key.
rsub:s3_compatible.expert: A custom S3 service: its https address, a signing region if it needs one, bucket and optional prefix, and an access key.

field:phrase.title: Recovery phrase
field:phrase.text: The recovery key written in your Recovery Kit, like river candle orbit maple quiet lantern. It unlocks this backup. It's used once and never saved.
field:phrase.expert: The Backup Recovery Key from your Recovery Kit. It decrypts this backup repository; it's used for this restore and not stored.

group:pick.title: Choose what to bring back
group:pick.text: Each copy is a moment the backup was taken. The newest is usually the right one.
group:pick.expert: Each entry is a snapshot of the backup repository at the time it was taken. The newest is usually the one you want.

elsewhere.title: Look somewhere else
elsewhere.text: Go back and point to another place the backup might be.
elsewhere.expert: Return to the source step; the reached place, unlock and pick are dropped when another place is chosen.

group:pickProject.title: Your Projects
group:pickProject.text: Everything that came back. Pick the one to open first.
group:pickProject.expert: The restored Projects; the one you pick opens first.

createNew.title: Create a new Project
createNew.text: Starts something new instead. Your restored Projects are all still there.
createNew.expert: Starts a new Project draft instead; the restored Projects stay as they are.

pick:new.title: New Project
pick:new.text: Puppet Master makes an empty folder for it and keeps saved versions from the start, so you can go back to earlier work.
pick:new.expert: A new, empty Project folder with local version control (Git or Jujutsu) from the start.

pick:existing.title: Existing work
pick:existing.text: A folder on this computer, a Project stored online like GitHub, or files on another device. Puppet Master reads it but changes nothing until you create the Project.
pick:existing.expert: Import existing work: a local folder, a remote repository on an online service, or files on another device (SSH, SMB, NFS or a mounted drive). Read only until the Project is created.

pick:restore.title: Restore
pick:restore.text: Brings a Project back from one of your backups.
pick:restore.expert: Restore a Project from a backup repository.

sub:folder.title: A folder on this computer
sub:folder.text: Work already in a folder on the computer doing the work. Pick the folder next; it is only read until you create the Project.
sub:folder.expert: A local folder on the machine doing the work; read only until the Project is created.

sub:online.title: A Project stored online
sub:online.text: Work kept on a website like GitHub or GitLab. Sign in and pick it; the next steps show where your working copy will live.
sub:online.expert: Clone a remote repository from an online service; the next steps say where the working copy will live.

sub:device.title: Files on another device
sub:device.text: Work on a NAS, a network drive or another computer. Puppet Master works on it right where it is.
sub:device.expert: Files on a NAS, a network share or another computer, used where they are (SSH/SFTP, SMB, NFS or a mounted drive).

later.title: Set up a Project later
later.text: No Project is created now; make one whenever you like. Setup finishes without one.
later.expert: No Project draft is created now; setup finishes without one, and you can create one later.

group:pick.title: Recent folders
group:pick.text: Folders you used lately. Puppet Master reads the one you pick but changes nothing until you create the Project.
group:pick.expert: Recently used folders. The one you pick is read only until the Project is created.

browse.title: Browse
browse.text: Look through your folders and choose any one, if it is not in the list.
browse.expert: Browse the file system for any folder.

group:treeGo.title: Choose a folder
group:treeGo.text: Open folders to look inside. When you are in the right one, use Choose this folder.
group:treeGo.expert: Navigate into a folder, then Choose this folder.

field:name.title: Project name
field:name.text: The name shown for this Project in Puppet Master. For a new Project it also names its folder. An existing folder keeps its own name and place.
field:name.expert: The Project's display name. For a new Project it also names the folder; an existing folder keeps its own name and path.

group:suggest.title: Suggestions
group:suggest.text: A few example names to start from. Pick one, then change any word you like.
group:suggest.expert: Example names; pick one and edit it.

change.title: Where its files live
change.text: Shows where the folder will be kept. Change picks another folder here, or a network drive.
change.expert: Where the Project folder is created: the default location, another folder, or a network location.

loc:auto.title: On this computer
loc:auto.text: In Puppet Master's own folder in Documents. Easy to find, and right for most people.
loc:auto.expert: The default location: Puppet Master's folder in Documents.

loc:custom.title: Another folder on this computer
loc:custom.text: Keep it in a folder you choose, like one you already use for this kind of work.
loc:custom.expert: A folder path you choose on this computer.

loc:network.title: A network drive or NAS
loc:network.text: Keep the files on a storage device on your network. Uses a secure connection (SSH) by default.
loc:network.expert: A network location (a NAS or share), reached over SSH by default.

field:custom.title: Choose a folder
field:custom.text: The folder path to use, like ~/Documents/Clubs. The ~ means your own home folder.
field:custom.expert: The folder path, like ~/Documents/Clubs (~ is your home folder).

storage:with_server.title: On your Server
storage:with_server.text: Recommended. The Server keeps the files next to the work, so nothing waits on this device.
storage:with_server.expert: The Project's files live on the Server's own storage, next to the agent runs. Recommended.

storage:this_device.title: On this device
storage:this_device.text: Files stay on this device and the Server reaches them over the network. This device needs to be on while it works.
storage:this_device.expert: The files stay on this device and the Server reaches them over the network; this device must stay on and reachable while the Server works.

storage:network_location.title: A network drive
storage:network_location.text: A NAS or shared folder on your network keeps the files, and the Server works on them there.
storage:network_location.expert: A NAS or network share holds the files and the Server works on them there (SSH, SMB or NFS).

pick:fresh.title: Start fresh
pick:fresh.text: Puppet Master's standard settings. Right for a first Project, or when you want a clean start.
pick:fresh.expert: Puppet Master's default settings for a new Project.

group:pick.title: Like another Project
group:pick.text: Reuses the settings of a Project you already trust. Never copied: sign-ins and keys, files, history, Goals and Plans.
group:pick.expert: Copies the chosen Project's settings into the new one. Never copied: credentials and keys, files, history, Goals and Plans.

choose.title: Choose settings
choose.text: Pick which groups of settings come along, like look, notifications or AI accounts.
choose.expert: Choose which settings categories are copied.

group:cat.title: Settings to copy
group:cat.text: Each group is a set of settings from that Project. Switch one off to keep the standard ones for it.
group:cat.expert: A settings category from the source Project; switch it off to keep the defaults for it.

pick:github.title: GitHub
pick:github.text: The most used website for keeping projects online, free for private Projects. Pick it if you're not sure.
pick:github.expert: GitHub.com: hosted Git remote, private repositories on free plans, browser sign-in. The default service.

pick:gitlab.title: GitLab
pick:gitlab.text: A website like GitHub. Pick it if you or your team already use GitLab, on gitlab.com or on your own server.
pick:gitlab.expert: GitLab.com or a self-managed GitLab: a Git remote with projects in groups; a self-managed instance needs its https address.

pick:azure_devops.title: Azure DevOps
pick:azure_devops.text: Microsoft's service for teams at work. Pick it if your workplace keeps its projects there.
pick:azure_devops.expert: Azure DevOps Services (dev.azure.com) or Azure DevOps Server: Git repositories (Azure Repos) inside an organisation and a team project, chosen on the next screen.

pick:bitbucket_cloud.title: Bitbucket
pick:bitbucket_cloud.text: Atlassian's website for keeping projects online, often used alongside Jira. Pick it if your team uses Bitbucket.
pick:bitbucket_cloud.expert: Bitbucket Cloud (workspaces) or Bitbucket Data Center (self-hosted, needs its address): a Git remote.

pick:forgejo.title: Forgejo
pick:forgejo.text: A free service people run on their own servers. Codeberg is the best-known one. Pick it if you have an account on Codeberg or another Forgejo server.
pick:forgejo.expert: Codeberg (browser sign-in or a token) or another Forgejo instance at its https address (a personal access token).

pick:gitea.title: Gitea
pick:gitea.text: A small service people run on their own servers, or rent as Gitea Cloud. Pick it if your team already uses one.
pick:gitea.expert: Gitea Cloud at your team's own address (browser sign-in or a token), or a self-hosted Gitea at its https address (a personal access token).

pick:github_enterprise.title: GitHub Enterprise
pick:github_enterprise.text: GitHub run by your company on its own server. Pick it if your company gave you its address.
pick:github_enterprise.expert: GitHub Enterprise Server (self-managed): needs its https address; you sign in on that server.

pick:cursor_origin.title: Cursor Origin
pick:cursor_origin.text: Cursor's own service for keeping projects online. It is still a preview, so it may change.
pick:cursor_origin.expert: Cursor Origin (preview): a Git remote hosted by Cursor. Expect changes while it is a preview.

notNow.title: Not now
notNow.text: No online copy for now. Earlier versions stay on this computer with Safe History, and you can add an online copy later in Settings.
notNow.expert: No remote: the repository stays local. Add a remote later in Settings.

group:variant.title: Which edition
group:variant.text: The same service, run in different places: by the company itself, by your organisation on its own server, or (for Forgejo and Gitea) on a server someone else runs. Pick the one your account is on.
group:variant.expert: Hosted (the vendor runs it), self-managed / Data Center (your organisation runs it at its own https address), Codeberg for hosted Forgejo, Gitea Cloud (a dedicated instance per team, at its own address).

field:address.title: Server address
field:address.text: Where that server lives, starting with https://, like https://git.example.com. For Gitea Cloud, the address your team was given.
field:address.expert: The instance's base URL (https only, a path such as /git is kept), used for its sign-in and API. Never filled in for you.

group:pick.title: Which online service
group:pick.text: These websites keep an online copy of your Project. They all keep it the same way, so the choice is about where you or your team already have an account. If you don't have one, pick GitHub: it's free for private Projects.
group:pick.expert: The forge that hosts the remote repository and its access. Local history (Git or Jujutsu) is separate; every forge here takes a Git push. Sign-in is per service: a browser sign-in on most, a personal access token on Forgejo and Gitea.

others.title: Which service to pick
others.text: These websites keep an online copy of your Project, and they all keep it the same way. The difference is where you or your team already have an account. If you don't have one, GitHub is the safe choice: it's free for private Projects.
others.expert: Every service here hosts a Git remote for your local history (Git or Jujutsu). Choose by where your account, organisation or self-managed instance already is. Sign-in differs: a browser sign-in on most, a personal access token on Forgejo and Gitea. Without a reason to pick another, use GitHub.com.

group:useKnown.title: Use this account
group:useKnown.text: This computer is already signed in to this account. What it allows depends on the service and on what you approved when you signed in.
group:useKnown.expert: An account this computer is already signed in to for this service; the token or grant it has is reused. The permissions it gives depend on the service and how it was approved.

another.title: Use a different account
another.text: Sign in with another account instead, like a work one.
another.expert: Sign in with a different account on this service instead.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.text: Opens its sign-in page in your browser. Sign in there and check the access it asks for before you approve, then come back.
signIn.expert: Opens the service's own sign-in page in your browser (OAuth); you approve the access it asks for there. Nothing to type here.

create.title: Create account
create.text: No account yet? Opens its sign-up page. Make the account there, then sign in here.
create.expert: Opens the service's sign-up page; sign in here once the account exists.

tokenOn.title: Use an access token instead
tokenOn.text: A token is a long password made just for apps. Use it if you'd rather not sign in in the browser, or your server asks for one.
tokenOn.expert: Personal access token, scoped as listed under the box for this purpose (make a copy, or bring one in). Kept by the keychain owner; the plan records only that a token is used (auth_method pat_ref).

field:token.title: Access token
field:token.text: Make it on the server with the permissions listed under the box, then paste it here. It stays in your computer's password store.
field:token.expert: A PAT with the least scopes for this purpose, kept by the credential owner; the plan records only that a token is used.

code.title: Browser didn't open?
code.text: Shows a short code instead. Open the address it gives on any device and type the code there.
code.expert: Device-code sign-in: open the address shown on any device and enter the code there.

copyLink.title: Browser didn't open?
copyLink.text: Copies the sign-in link, so you can paste it into your browser yourself.
copyLink.expert: Copies the sign-in URL to open in a browser yourself.

copy:dcode.title: Copy the code
copy:dcode.text: Copies this sign-in code. Paste it on the page named above.
copy:dcode.expert: Copies the device code for the page named above.

newCode.title: New code
newCode.text: Makes a fresh code if this one ran out. Codes last 15 minutes.
newCode.expert: Issues a new device code; each lasts 15 minutes.

signupBack.title: Back to sign in
signupBack.text: Made your account on its page? Choose this, then sign in with it.
signupBack.expert: Return to sign-in once the new account exists.

field:repo.title: Name on the service
field:repo.text: How the online copy is named there. If a name won't work on that service, the line under the box says why.
field:repo.expert: Checked with the provider's own rule (GitHub, GitLab path, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket slug, Forgejo/Gitea), not one shared pattern.

group:owner.title: Where it lives
group:owner.text: Your own account, or a place you share with others: an organization, group, workspace or project. Pick the one the Project belongs to.
group:owner.expert: Owner or namespace in the provider's terms: user or organization, GitLab group/subgroup, Azure DevOps organization or collection, Bitbucket workspace, Data Center project key, Origin team.

group:azOrg.title: Organization
group:azOrg.text: The Azure DevOps organization the Project belongs to.
group:azOrg.expert: The Azure DevOps organisation that will own the repository.

group:azProject.title: Team project
group:azProject.text: Azure DevOps groups work into team projects. Pick one marked Git. It's Azure DevOps' own grouping, separate from your Puppet Master Project.
group:azProject.expert: The Azure DevOps team project that will hold the Git repository (Azure Repos); separate from your Puppet Master Project.

azRefresh.title: Refresh projects
azRefresh.text: Looks again for team projects, like one you just made on Azure DevOps.
azRefresh.expert: Lists the organisation's team projects again, like one you just created.

azCreateTeamProject.title: Create a team project
azCreateTeamProject.text: Opens Azure DevOps to make a new team project there. Come back and refresh to pick it.
azCreateTeamProject.expert: Opens Azure DevOps to create a team project there; refresh here to pick it.

vis:private.title: Only you
vis:private.text: Only you, and people you give access, can see it. Right for most Projects.
vis:private.expert: private: visible to the owner and explicitly granted members (on Bitbucket Data Center, the project's permissions).

vis:public.title: Everyone
vis:public.text: Anyone on the internet can see it and copy it; only you and people you invite can change it. Pick it only for work you mean to share.
vis:public.expert: Public repository: anyone can read and clone it; only collaborators can push.

vis:internal.title: A wider group
vis:internal.text: More people than just you, but nobody outside: your company on GitHub, everyone signed in to a GitLab server, or your team on Cursor Origin.
vis:internal.expert: internal: GitHub enterprise members; GitLab self-managed signed-in users (not GitLab.com); Origin team members. Never for a personal owner, Forgejo, Gitea or Bitbucket.

field:desc.title: Description
field:desc.text: A sentence about the Project, shown on its online page. Optional.
field:desc.expert: The repository description shown on the service. Optional.

field:branch.title: Main branch name
field:branch.text: The name of the main line of your work, usually main. Leave it unless your team uses another name. No spaces.
field:branch.expert: The default branch, checked as git check-ref-format --branch does (no .., @{, spaces, ~ ^ : ? * [ \, leading -, trailing / or .).

readme.title: Add a README file
readme.text: Adds a short page that says what the Project is: the first thing people see online.
readme.expert: Initialises the repository with a README.md.

group:gitignore.title: Files to leave out
group:gitignore.text: Skips common temporary files when saving versions. Keep Chosen for you if unsure. It doesn't guarantee that private information stays out of your saved versions.
group:gitignore.expert: A .gitignore template: patterns Git won't track, like build output and temporary files. It isn't a secrets filter.

group:license.title: License
group:license.text: Sets the terms for reusing work you share. No license keeps all rights with you. Leave it unchanged if unsure, and read a license's terms before you publish with it.
group:license.expert: The LICENSE file added to the repository: the terms for reusing the code. No license reserves all rights.

group:bbProject.title: Project
group:bbProject.text: Bitbucket keeps every copy in one of the workspace's projects. A private project holds only private copies.
group:bbProject.expert: Bitbucket Cloud project key, chosen explicitly (the API would otherwise use the workspace's oldest project). Private projects hold only private repositories.

field:q.title: Search your Projects
field:q.text: Type part of a name to find it quickly.

group:pick.title: Choose the Project
group:pick.text: Only the Project you pick is copied, along with where it lives on the service. The line below shows where the working copy will be kept.
group:pick.expert: The selected repository's provider id, owner and (Azure DevOps team project, Bitbucket project) container are carried into the plan, so nothing has to be entered again.

group:backend.title: Git or Jujutsu
group:backend.text: Both keep earlier versions of your Project on this computer, with no account. Git is the usual choice; pick it if you're not sure. Jujutsu can also undo any step. One of them is always on: 'Not now' below is only about an online copy.
group:backend.expert: Local version control, always Git or Jujutsu for a Project made here. Jujutsu runs colocated with Git, so any Git remote works with either, and its operation log makes every step undoable (jj undo).

backend:git.title: Git
backend:git.text: The usual way to keep versions. Every online service and most tools work with it. Pick it if you're not sure.
backend:git.expert: Git: commits, branches and the staging index. Pushes to every supported service. The default backend.

backend:jujutsu.title: Jujutsu
backend:jujutsu.text: Records every change as you go and can undo any step, even an undo. It saves in Git's format, so GitHub and the other services still work. Pick it if you like trying things and stepping back.
backend:jujutsu.expert: Jujutsu (jj): working-copy-as-a-commit, stable change IDs, bookmarks for branches, and an operation log with jj undo and jj op restore. Colocated with .git, so Git remotes and tools keep working.

filesafe.title: FileSafe
filesafe.text: Guards your files while the AI works: it stops risky commands, keeps changes inside this Project, keeps passwords out, and copies a file before changing it. This one switch covers all of it; Settings has each part on its own. Leave it on.
filesafe.expert: The guard layer for agent runs: command blocklist, write scope, security filter, and pre-write safe points before a file is overwritten; blocks are logged. This switch turns all of them on or off together; each has its own setting in Settings.

online.title: Online copy
online.text: A copy of your Project on a website such as GitHub: a second copy, and a way to work from another computer or share it. Only you see it unless you share it.
online.expert: A remote repository on the service you choose, pushed from your local history; its visibility is set when it is created.

backup.title: Backup
backup.text: A separate full copy of your Project kept somewhere else, so you can bring it back if this computer is lost or broken. Your Recovery Kit file opens it, so keep that file somewhere other than this computer.
backup.expert: An independent, encrypted backup repository at the destination you pick (a NAS over SSH, Google Drive, OneDrive, an S3 or B2 bucket, SFTP or WebDAV), restorable with the Recovery Kit. It is separate from the online copy and from local history.

bdest:nas.title: Home NAS
bdest:nas.text: A storage box on your home network keeps the backup. Close by and quick, but at home: it doesn't help if your home is the problem.
bdest:nas.expert: A backup repository on your NAS, reached over SSH (or through its Puppet Master when it runs one). Encrypted before it leaves the work computer.

bdest:gdrive.title: Google Drive
bdest:gdrive.text: Keeps the backup in your Google account. You'll sign in right after your Project is created.
bdest:gdrive.expert: An encrypted backup repository in your Google Drive, through Google's sign-in (OAuth) after the Project is created.

bdest:onedrive.title: OneDrive
bdest:onedrive.text: Keeps the backup in your Microsoft account. You'll sign in right after your Project is created.
bdest:onedrive.expert: An encrypted backup repository in your OneDrive, through Microsoft's sign-in (OAuth) after the Project is created.

bdest:s3.title: A storage bucket
bdest:s3.text: Cloud storage you rent, like Amazon S3 or Backblaze B2. Pick the service under the card; you add its access details after your Project is created.
bdest:s3.expert: Object storage: Amazon S3, Backblaze B2 (its S3 API, regional address, application key) or another S3 service at its own address. Keys are added after the Project is created.

bdest:sftp.title: Another server
bdest:sftp.text: A server you can reach over SFTP or WebDAV, like one at work or a friend's. Pick which under the card.
bdest:sftp.expert: sftp (SSH file transfer at sftp://host/path; its host key is checked) or webdav (HTTPS, https://host/path, e.g. Nextcloud). Recorded as its own family.

bdest:none.title: Not now
bdest:none.text: No separate backup for now. Earlier versions stay on this computer with Safe History, so if this computer is lost, the Project is lost too unless it has an online copy. You can add a backup later in Settings.
bdest:none.expert: No backup destination. Local history and any remote stay as they are; nothing protects against losing this computer except a remote. Add a destination later in Settings.

bsub:aws_s3.title: Amazon S3
bsub:aws_s3.text: Amazon's storage. You'll need the bucket's name and an access key made for it.
bsub:aws_s3.expert: AWS S3: bucket name (3-63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes), region discovered from the bucket; access key ID and secret, plus a session token for temporary credentials.

bsub:backblaze_b2.title: Backblaze B2
bsub:backblaze_b2.text: Backblaze's storage. You'll need the bucket's S3 address, shown on its page, and an application key made for that bucket.
bsub:backblaze_b2.expert: Backblaze B2 through its S3-compatible API: s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com, an application key ID and key (the master application key is refused there); bucket names 6-63 characters.

bsub:s3_compatible.title: S3-compatible storage
bsub:s3_compatible.text: Any other storage that works like Amazon's, such as Wasabi or MinIO. You'll need its address, the bucket and a key.
bsub:s3_compatible.expert: A custom S3 service: its https address, a signing region if it needs one, bucket and optional prefix, and an access key.

bsub:sftp.title: SFTP
bsub:sftp.text: A server you sign in to with a username and password over a secure connection.
bsub:sftp.expert: SFTP over SSH: sftp://host[:port]/path; the host key is checked at the test.

bsub:webdav.title: WebDAV
bsub:webdav.text: A folder on a web server, like Nextcloud, reached at an https address.
bsub:webdav.expert: WebDAV over HTTPS (RFC 4918): the collection's https address; its certificate is checked.

pick:home.title: Only at home
pick:home.text: Your devices reach the Server on your home network, or on a private network you already use, called a VPN. Nothing is opened to the internet.
pick:home.expert: LAN or an existing VPN only; no remote route is configured and nothing is exposed publicly.

pick:anywhere.title: Away from home
pick:anywhere.text: Tailscale is a private network for your own devices, built into Puppet Master. Sign in once, after you confirm, and the Puppet Master app on your other devices can use it. In a plain web browser, use Remote Link or that device's own Tailscale.
pick:anywhere.expert: Built-in Tailscale connector on the Server and in Puppet Master's own apps; sign in once after Review. A plain browser tab needs Remote Link or the device's own Tailscale.

route:headscale.title: My own Headscale server
route:headscale.text: Like Tailscale, but run on a server of your own. Pick it only if you already run Headscale. Whoever runs it approves your Server.
route:headscale.expert: Self-hosted Headscale control server; the connector enrolls after Review by interactive approval or a one-time key. No Funnel.

route:reverse_proxy.title: My own web address
route:reverse_proxy.text: Puts your Server at a web address you own, like pm.example.com, on the internet. Anyone can find its sign-in page; only devices you pair can use it. Puppet Master writes the settings for your proxy.
route:reverse_proxy.expert: Public custom-domain route through your reverse proxy (dedicated hostname). Puppet Master generates the proxy configuration; DNS, inbound HTTPS and certificates are yours. Explicit consent; route tests run after Review.

route:remote_link.title: Puppet Master Remote Link
route:remote_link.text: Your Server makes a link for your other devices. No account, web address or router changes. Each device still needs your approval.
route:remote_link.expert: Accountless outbound rendezvous (direct or relayed). The Server creates the link after Review; pairing is still required.

field:proxy.title: Web address
field:proxy.text: The address you own, like https://pm.example.com. It needs a name of its own, with nothing after it.
field:proxy.expert: Dedicated https origin for the proxy; no subpath, credentials, query or fragment.

hosting:generate_only.title: Make the settings file
hosting:generate_only.text: Puppet Master writes the settings file for your proxy, the program that answers on your web address. You add it to your proxy; certificates stay on your side.
hosting:generate_only.expert: Exports a Caddy, NGINX or Traefik configuration for this origin; you install it. TLS stays with your proxy (Caddy's automatic HTTPS, or your certificate where the file marks it).

hosting:existing_proxy.title: I have one already
hosting:existing_proxy.text: Your address already points at a proxy you run, such as Nginx Proxy Manager. Puppet Master checks it reaches your Server.
hosting:existing_proxy.expert: Existing external proxy: Puppet Master tests the route to the Server; nothing is generated and certificates stay yours.

group:kind.title: Which proxy
group:kind.text: Which proxy the settings file is for. Caddy is the default and gets its certificate by itself. Using Nginx Proxy Manager? Choose I have one already.
group:kind.expert: Configuration target: Caddy (default, automatic HTTPS), NGINX or Traefik (the file marks the certificate and key paths). Nginx Proxy Manager is an existing proxy.

field:headscale.title: Headscale address
field:headscale.text: The https:// address of your Headscale server, like https://headscale.example.com.

group:edit.title: Edit
group:edit.text: Goes back to change this choice. Your Project hasn't been created yet.
group:edit.expert: Returns to that step to change it; nothing has been created yet.

retry.title: Try again
retry.text: Tries the unfinished step again. Work that already finished is kept.
retry.expert: Retries the failed step with the same attempt; completed steps aren't repeated.

rename.title: Change the name
rename.text: Pick another name for the online copy, since that one is already used there.
rename.expert: The repository name is taken on the service: choose another name and the attempt resumes.

skipOnline.title: Skip the online copy
skipOnline.text: Finish without the online copy. You can add one later from Settings.
skipOnline.expert: Finishes without creating the remote repository; add a remote later in Settings.

askSkip.title: Skip the online copy
askSkip.text: Finish without the online copy. You can add one later from Settings.
askSkip.expert: Finishes without creating the remote repository; add a remote later in Settings.

confirmDelete.title: Delete the online copy
confirmDelete.text: Deletes only the online copy named here. This can't be undone; your files here are kept.
confirmDelete.expert: Deletes only the remote repository named here, on the service. Irreversible; local files are kept.

cancelDelete.title: Keep it
cancelDelete.text: Keeps the online copy and returns to the recovery choices.
cancelDelete.expert: Keeps the remote repository and returns to the recovery choices.

continueSetup.title: Continue Setup
continueSetup.text: Picks up the setup where it stopped, using the online copy that was already made.
continueSetup.expert: Resumes the setup from where it stopped, binding the remote repository that was already created.

openRepo.title: Open the online copy
openRepo.text: Opens the online copy on its website, so you can see what was made.
openRepo.expert: Opens the created remote repository on the service.

deleteRepo.title: Delete the online copy
deleteRepo.text: Deletes only the online copy, and can't be undone. Your files here are not touched.
deleteRepo.expert: Deletes only the remote repository on the service; irreversible. Local files are not touched.

checkAgain.title: Check again
checkAgain.text: Asks the service again how the setup went. Nothing is retried or deleted on its own.
checkAgain.expert: Asks the service again for the outcome of the setup; nothing is retried or deleted on its own.

reviewAgain.title: Review setup again
reviewAgain.text: Goes back to the review to start a fresh attempt. The old one is never reused.
reviewAgain.expert: Back to Review for a fresh attempt with a new idempotency key; the old attempt is never reused.

step:signin.title: Sign in or connect
step:signin.text: Lets Puppet Master reach the place your backups go. You do it once.
step:signin.expert: Authenticates to the backup destination once: SSH to the NAS, the service's sign-in, or the bucket's access key.

step:test.title: Run a quick test
step:test.text: Makes a small backup and reads it back, to prove it works before you rely on it.
step:test.expert: Writes a small test backup to the destination and reads it back before anything relies on it.

step:kit.title: Save your Recovery Kit
step:kit.text: Your Recovery Kit holds the key that unlocks your backups, not the backup itself. Keep a copy somewhere you can reach if this computer is lost, like a password manager. Anyone with the kit and the backup can open it. If every copy is lost, Puppet Master can't open the backup.
step:kit.expert: Delivers the Backup Recovery Key in your Recovery Kit (save, copy or print), once. There is no escrow: if every copy of the key is lost, the backups can't be decrypted. Keep it off the computer it protects.

step:kitTest.title: Check your Recovery Kit
step:kitTest.text: Opens the backup with the kit you saved, so you know it is the right one before you need it.
step:kitTest.expert: Proves the saved kit unlocks the backup repository read-only before you need it.

step:policy.title: Turn on daily backups
step:policy.text: Turns on automatic backups on a schedule, run while the computer doing the work and the backup place can be reached.
step:policy.expert: Enables the backup schedule for this Project; runs happen while the work computer and the destination are reachable.

stepUp.title: Confirm it's you
stepUp.text: The kit is shown only to you, once, on this device. This makes sure it is really you asking.
stepUp.expert: A step-up confirmation before the Recovery Kit is shown: it is shown once, on this device, only to you.

later.title: Do this later
later.text: Your Project is ready either way. Backups stay off until you finish these steps.
later.expert: The Project is ready either way; the backup stays off until these steps are finished.

bsub:aws_s3.title: Amazon S3
bsub:aws_s3.text: Amazon's storage. You'll need the bucket's name and an access key made for it.
bsub:aws_s3.expert: AWS S3: bucket name (3-63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes), region discovered from the bucket; access key ID and secret, plus a session token for temporary credentials.

bsub:backblaze_b2.title: Backblaze B2
bsub:backblaze_b2.text: Backblaze's storage. You'll need the bucket's S3 address, shown on its page, and an application key made for that bucket.
bsub:backblaze_b2.expert: Backblaze B2 through its S3-compatible API: s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com, an application key ID and key (the master application key is refused there); bucket names 6-63 characters.

bsub:s3_compatible.title: S3-compatible storage
bsub:s3_compatible.text: Any other storage that works like Amazon's, such as Wasabi or MinIO. You'll need its address, the bucket and a key.
bsub:s3_compatible.expert: A custom S3 service: its https address, a signing region if it needs one, bucket and optional prefix, and an access key.

bsub:sftp.title: SFTP
bsub:sftp.text: A server you sign in to with a username and password over a secure connection.
bsub:sftp.expert: SFTP over SSH: sftp://host[:port]/path; the host key is checked at the test.

bsub:webdav.title: WebDAV
bsub:webdav.text: A folder on a web server, like Nextcloud, reached at an https address.
bsub:webdav.expert: WebDAV over HTTPS (RFC 4918): the collection's https address; its certificate is checked.

accTemp.title: Temporary keys
accTemp.text: Keys that expire, such as ones from a company sign-in, come with a session token. Add it if yours has one.
accTemp.expert: AWS STS temporary credentials: access key ID, secret access key and session token, all three sent through the credential owner.

all.title: See all providers
all.text: The full list, in three groups: plans you pay for, keys billed by what you use, and your own server. An AI provider is the company your assistant uses.
all.expert: All providers in this concept, grouped as subscriptions, API billing, and self-run servers.

none.title: I don't have any of these
none.text: No AI account yet? Shows the kinds there are, so you can pick one that suits you.
none.expert: Help choosing a first provider: a subscription, an API account, or free models.

skip.title: Skip for now
skip.text: Puppet Master can't plan or work until an AI is added. Add one any time from Settings.
skip.expert: Continues without a provider; planning and agent runs need one. Add it later in Settings.

free.title: Set Up Free Models
free.text: Adds free options with limits for suitable tasks. Their limits can change. Your paid accounts are used first by default; change that in Settings.
free.expert: Adds Free Models routes, each set up through its own provider's account. Paid accounts are preferred by default; the priorities are in Settings.

group:install.title: Install
group:install.text: This AI needs its own app on the computer that does the work. Puppet Master installs it with the maker's official installer, only when you choose Install.
group:install.expert: Explicit, consented install of the vendor CLI on the exact execution host from its official source; the CLI then owns its sign-in there.

field:q.title: Search
field:q.text: Type a name, like Claude, Gemini or OpenCode, to find it quickly.

pick:sub.title: A monthly plan
pick:sub.text: A plan you subscribe to, like Claude or ChatGPT.
pick:sub.expert: A subscription account (Claude, ChatGPT and others).

pick:api.title: Pay as you go
pick:api.text: Like the Anthropic or Gemini API. You pay for what you use, so the cost goes up and down with how much you use it.
pick:api.expert: A pay-as-you-go API account (Anthropic API, Gemini API): billed per token, authenticated with an API key.

pick:free.title: Free Models
pick:free.text: Free options with limits. Good for trying things out before you pay for anything.
pick:free.expert: Free model routes with rate limits and changing availability; useful to try things out.

group:signup.title: Sign-up pages
group:signup.text: Opens that company's own sign-up page in your browser. When you come back, it's at the top of the list.
group:signup.expert: Opens the provider's sign-up page; on return the AI step lists that provider first.

route:free-openrouter.title: OpenRouter free models
route:free-openrouter.text: OpenRouter's free models: free to use, with a small daily limit. You sign in on OpenRouter's page.
route:free-openrouter.expert: OpenRouter :free model variants through OpenRouter sign-in; per-minute and per-day request limits depend on credit bought.

route:free-github-models.title: GitHub Models
route:free-github-models.text: GitHub closed this service. Choose another route.
route:free-github-models.expert: GitHub Models was fully retired on July 30, 2026; shown only as No longer available for a saved choice.

route:free-groq.title: Groq free plan
route:free-groq.text: Groq's free plan, with limits. Get a key from Groq's console. When a limit is reached, it waits for it to reset.
route:free-groq.expert: Groq Free plan with a Groq API key; a 429 carries retry-after and reset headers. Retry now, never a reconnect.

attribution.title: Where this list comes from
attribution.text: The free model list is based on a community list. Opens it in your browser.
attribution.expert: The free route list is based on a community-maintained list; opens it in your browser.

route:free-nvidia.title: NVIDIA free models
route:free-nvidia.text: Free AI models from NVIDIA, with limits. Get a key from NVIDIA's API catalog.
route:free-nvidia.expert: NVIDIA API catalog (NIM) endpoints with free inference for listed models; an NVIDIA API key; rate limits apply.

group:route.title: Free option
group:route.text: A free option from the community list. Set it up with that company's key or sign-in, or just turn it on where none is needed.
group:route.expert: A free route from free-coding-models (v0.6.0), set up through its own provider's key, sign-in, or no credential; limits are the provider's.

summary:free.title: Free Models
summary:free.text: Free options with limits, good for trying things out.
summary:free.expert: Free model routes with rate limits.

summary:backup.title: Backup
summary:backup.text: A separate copy of your Project kept somewhere else, so you can get it back if this computer is lost. Saved versions on the same computer can be lost with it. Not set up yet? Add one in Settings.
summary:backup.expert: An encrypted backup repository at another destination. Not set up yet? Add one in Settings.

createNow.title: Create a Project now
createNow.text: Goes back to make your first Project now. What you already set up stays as it is.
createNow.expert: Returns to Begin to create the first Project now; what's already set up is kept.

method:ssh.title: SSH
method:ssh.text: Recommended. A secure way to reach the device. Puppet Master uses a key, so no password is kept.
method:ssh.expert: SSH (SFTP for files), with a key; host identity checked first. Recommended.

method:smb.title: SMB
method:smb.text: Windows and Mac file sharing. Pick it for a shared folder you already open from your computer.
method:smb.expert: SMB (CIFS) file sharing, as Windows and macOS mount it.

method:nfs.title: NFS
method:nfs.text: File sharing many NAS devices and Linux computers use. Pick it if your device shares that way.
method:nfs.expert: An NFS export from the NAS or a Linux machine.

method:mounted.title: Already connected
method:mounted.text: A drive the computer doing the work already has connected. Nothing more to connect.
method:mounted.expert: An existing OS mount on the computer that does the work (this computer, or the Server); no new credentials.

group:device.title: Choose a device
group:device.text: Devices Puppet Master found on your network. Nothing is changed by looking.
group:device.expert: Devices found on your network by read-only discovery.

field:addr.title: Address
field:addr.text: Where to reach the device, like 192.168.1.20 or nas.local.
field:addr.expert: The device's hostname or IP address, like 192.168.1.20 or nas.local.

field:port.title: Port
field:port.text: The door number SSH answers on, from 1 to 65535. Leave it at 22 unless whoever set up the device changed it.
field:port.expert: SSH TCP port, 1–65535 (default 22). Changing it means the device's identity is checked again.

manualOn.title: Type an address instead
manualOn.text: Enter its address yourself if the device does not show up.
manualOn.expert: Enter the device's hostname or IP address yourself.

group:share.title: Shared folders found
group:share.text: Folders the device shares on your network. Pick the one with the files.
group:share.expert: SMB or NFS shares the device exports.

group:volume.title: Connected drives
group:volume.text: Drives the computer doing the work already has connected. Pick the one with the files.
group:volume.expert: Existing mounts on the connecting computer (this computer, or the Server); the next step checks it can read them.

field:shareText.title: Shared folder address
field:shareText.text: Type where the shared folder is if it wasn't found: //computer/folder for a shared folder, or computer:/path for NFS.
field:shareText.expert: SMB UNC path (//host/share) or NFS export (host:/path), opened from the computer that does the work.

shareManual:on.title: Type its address instead
shareManual:on.text: For a shared folder that didn't show up in the list.
shareManual:on.expert: Enter an SMB share or NFS export that discovery didn't list.

shareManual:off.title: Show the shares found
shareManual:off.text: Back to the shared folders Puppet Master found on your network.

trust.title: Yes, this is my device
trust.text: Check this device's identity using information you already trust, like its own settings or whoever set it up. Choose this only when they match. If you can't confirm it, stop.
trust.expert: Trusts this SSH host key after you compare its fingerprint (shown as a picture and words) with one you already trust, like the device's own settings or its owner.

trustNew.title: Trust the new ID
trustNew.text: Only if you reset the device yourself. Otherwise something may be pretending to be it, so stop.
trustNew.expert: Accepts a changed host key. Only after a reset or reinstall you made yourself; otherwise this may be a man-in-the-middle.

stop.title: Stop
stop.text: Stops here and connects to nothing. The safe choice when you didn't reset the device.
stop.expert: Stops without connecting; nothing is trusted.

group:pick.title: Choose a key
group:pick.text: A key lets Puppet Master connect without a password. Pick one marked Already works, or make a new key. Only the safe-to-share half of a key is read.
group:pick.expert: SSH keys on the computer that will connect (~/.ssh files and agent keys), each tested; only public keys are read.

pick:new.title: Make a new key
pick:new.text: A key just for Puppet Master. Easy to remove later, and it doesn't touch your other keys.
pick:new.expert: Generates an ed25519 key pair just for Puppet Master; easy to revoke, and other keys are untouched.

field:pass.title: Passphrase
field:pass.text: The password that locks this key. It unlocks the key on this computer and isn't saved.
field:pass.expert: The key's passphrase, to decrypt the private key on this computer; not stored.

field:sshUser.title: Account
field:sshUser.text: The account on the device that Puppet Master signs in to, usually your own. A key works for one account.
