field:sshUser.expert: Remote SSH user. Keys are tested and added for this account; another account is another connection.

userEdit.title: Change the account
userEdit.text: Sign in to the device as a different account. The keys are tested again for it.
userEdit.expert: Change the SSH user; key tests rerun for the new user@host:port.

field:user.title: Username
field:user.text: The account allowed to connect to this device with SSH. It can be different from the one for the device's web page; ask its owner if you don't know it.
field:user.expert: The SSH account on the device (it can differ from its web login).

field:pw.title: Password
field:pw.text: Used once to add your key. Never saved. After this, no password is needed.
field:pw.expert: The account's password, used once to install the public key into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys; not stored.

selfOn.title: I'll add the key myself
selfOn.text: Shows the line to add to the device yourself, so you never type your password here.
selfOn.expert: Shows the public key line to append to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the device yourself.

selfOff.title: Add it for me
selfOff.text: Puppet Master adds the key for you with your password, used once and never saved.
selfOff.expert: Puppet Master installs the public key for you, using the password once.

copy:pub.title: Copy the key line
copy:pub.text: Copies the public half of your key, the part that is safe to share, to add on the device.
copy:pub.expert: Copies the public key line (safe to share).

fixPerms.title: Fix the folder permissions
fixPerms.text: The device refused the key because its home folder is shared too widely. This tightens it so the key works.
fixPerms.expert: sshd refused the key because the home directory is group- or world-writable (StrictModes); this tightens those permissions.

useSsh.title: Use SSH instead
useSsh.text: Connect with a key instead of pairing. Only needed if you would rather not pair with its Puppet Master.
useSsh.expert: Use SSH with a key instead of pairing with the device's Puppet Master.

another.title: Choose another way
another.text: Pick a different way to approve this computer, like a code instead of a request.
another.expert: Choose another pairing method (code or QR instead of approval).

field:pmcode.title: Code from the device
field:pmcode.text: The 8 letters and numbers its Puppet Master shows, like A7K9-M2Q4.
field:pmcode.expert: The one-time pairing code the device's Puppet Master shows (8 characters).

resend.title: Send a new one
resend.text: Ends the request that went missing and sends a fresh one. Only the new one can be approved.
resend.expert: Cancels the current pairing request and starts a new one; an answer to the old request is ignored.

group:cd.title: Choose a folder
group:cd.text: Open folders to find the right one. Read-only folders cannot hold a Project.
group:cd.expert: Browse the device's folders over SFTP; a folder must be writable by the SSH account to hold a Project.

adding.title: New folder
adding.text: Makes a fresh folder for the Project. It is made when you create the Project.
adding.expert: Creates a new folder for the Project when the Project is created.

field:newName.title: Folder name
field:newName.text: A name for the new folder, like the Project name.

field:user.title: Username
field:user.text: The name you use for the shared folder. The computer doing the work keeps the sign-in in its own password store.
field:user.expert: SMB account on the share; the credential is held by the connecting computer's keychain or credential store.

field:pw.title: Password
field:pw.text: The password for the shared folder. The computer doing the work keeps it in its own password store, not Puppet Master.
field:pw.expert: SMB password, handed to the connecting computer's credential store; never saved by Puppet Master.

field:domain.title: Domain or workgroup
field:domain.text: Only on some work networks. Leave it empty at home.
field:domain.expert: Optional SMB domain/workgroup for the account (DOMAIN\user).

other.title: Choose another drive
other.text: Go back and pick a different connected drive.

start.title: Set it up
start.text: Starts setting up the way you chose to reach your Server away from home. Each step says what it is doing.
start.expert: Starts the Remote Access owner's setup for the reviewed route; each step is a separate owner command.

later.title: Do this later
later.text: Stops here without setting it up. Everything else keeps working at home. Finish it any time in Settings.
later.expert: Leaves the route not set up; Settings › Server & Project Location › Away From Home resumes it.

person:tsSignIn.title: Sign in to Tailscale
person:tsSignIn.text: Opens Tailscale's own sign-in page. Your Tailscale password is never typed into Puppet Master.
person:tsSignIn.expert: Opens Tailscale's protected authorization page; Puppet Master never sees the credentials.

person:hsApproved.title: It's approved
person:hsApproved.text: Press this once whoever runs your Headscale server has let your Server in.
person:hsApproved.expert: Continue after the Headscale administrator approves the node registration.

person:installed.title: I've added it
person:installed.text: Press this once the settings file is in your proxy. Puppet Master then checks it works.
person:installed.expert: Continue to the reach, certificate and live-connection tests after installing the exported configuration.

welcome.resumed: You're back! I kept your place.
welcome.returning: Welcome back. I found your things.

look.enter: Dress me up. It changes everything.
look.keep: Your look's kept. Change it if you like.
look.pickFamily:friendly: Soft and cosy. I like it.
look.pickFamily:glass: Ooh, shiny. Am I glass now?
look.pickFamily:retro: Retro! Straight out of an old computer.
look.pickMode:light: Light it is. Bright and clear.

where.enter: Where shall we do the work?
where.pick:server: A Server that stays on can work while you're away.
where.offline: No internet? Local work still works.

c-route.group:pickServer: That one? I'll string us together.
c-route.route:remote_link: A Remote Link? Paste it in.
c-route.typing: Type it in. I'll go and knock.

c-review.enter: It'll ask if it's really you.
c-review.pairing:approval: Tap approve on your other device.
c-review.pairing:code: A code! I love a secret.
c-review.pairing:qr: Say cheese to the QR code!

c-pair.waiting: Waiting for your OK over there…
c-pair.typing: Ooh, a code. Read it carefully.

c-ready.enter: Connected! Open one, or start fresh.
c-ready.empty: No Projects there yet. Make the first!
c-ready.createNew: Something new? I'll fetch a page.
c-ready.group:pickProject: Ooh, that one. Shall we open it?

s-kind.enter: What kind of computer will it be?
s-kind.kind:nas: A NAS that stays on. A good home.
s-kind.kind:pc: Another computer that stays on. Handy.

s-wait.enter: Waiting for it to show up…
s-wait.found: There it is! Shall we set it up?
s-wait.typing: An address! I'll go and look.

s-confirm.enter: Give it a name you'll know.
s-confirm.typing: Ooh, what shall we call it?
s-confirm.selfMatch: Same words? Then tick the box.

s-ready.enter: Your Server is ready! Bring friends.
s-ready.waiting: Someone wants in. Check the words.

r-source.source:kit: The Recovery Kit! The very best key.
r-source.source:folder: A folder, or a drive you plugged in.
r-source.source:nas: On the NAS? I'll go and fetch it.
r-source.source:cloud: Up in the cloud. I'll bring it down.
r-source.typing: Ooh, bucket details. I'll be careful.

r-unlock.typing: A secret phrase. I won't keep it.

r-pick.enter: Which copy shall we bring back?
r-pick.group:pick: That one? Newest is usually best.

r-preview.done: All back, just as it was.

begin.server: We'll keep it next to the work.
begin.pick:existing: Bring it in. I'll learn my way round.
begin.pick:restore: Back from the archive, good as new.
begin.sub:folder: A folder you already have. Easy.
begin.sub:device: On another device? I'll go and look.

ex-folder.hasHistory: It keeps its own history. Neat!
